Angular sectors have rank at most two. Direct disk integrals give A_m(L)=m²/((L+m)(L+2m)), cross-Gram G_pq(L)=pq/((L+p+q)sqrt((L+p)(L+q))), and determinant Δ=p²q²(p−q)²/[(L+p)(L+q)(L+2p)(L+2q)(L+p+q)²]>0. Thus for every nonnegative angular index the characteristic roots (τ±sqrt(τ²+4|η|²Δ))/2 have opposite signs, and remaining negative sectors are finite. Sum of squared Hankel column norms telescopes to m, proving trace class and Tr D=|η|²q−p; orthogonal radial complements give infinite-dimensional kernel. As L→∞, τ=sL⁻²+O(L⁻³), |η|²Δ=gL⁻⁶(1+O(1/L)), giving 2/4 tails when s≠0; at balance |η|=p/q cancellation leaves cubic roots with coefficients (p²/2)(sqrt(13)|p−q|±3(p−q)). Comparison with p-series gives strict Schatten cutoffs 1/2,1/4 or both 1/3. An independent rational Gram check across positive/negative angular sectors corroborated identities; infinite claims follow from the explicit expansions and summability, not the finite check.
